title: Personal, Local, Private AI Agents: Soumith Chintala
talk_summary: Soumith Chintala argues personal agents must run locally/privately because they hold intimate context and take powerful actions, and sketches a Mac Mini as the practical host. He lists technical gaps: slow local inference, weak computer-use, and no good 'catastrophic action classifiers' to stop irreversible mistakes.

takeaways.technique: Catastrophic-action classifier gate before irreversible operations
takeaways.what_they_do: Before an agent executes an action, a separate check classifies whether the action is reversible/harmless vs catastrophic, and escalates to a human instead of acting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't have good catastrophic action classifiers ... some actions that are actually catastrophic

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues an agent missing a context source (e.g. iMessage) confidently gives wrong answers, so partial-context agents are net-unusable because you can't tell when they're right.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a personal agent that doesn't have the right context it's largely going to be irritating to use

takeaways.technique: Dedicated always-on host for async agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Recommends a Mac Mini at home running agents asynchronously to avoid phone battery/OS restrictions and get persistent logins to services.

takeaways.technique: Open models improve faster per dollar; expect local/cheap tiers to close gap
takeaways.what_they_do: Claims open models compound across many contributors and improve faster per dollar than any single closed lab, so cheaper tiers become viable over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: open models are improving themselves like in coordination across board
